purpose: Full direct and symmetric TURN regression with the received-throughput backoff fix; retain phase-entry freeze accounting correction
scope: H.264 720p30, NACK/RTX/FlexFEC 5/1, zero requested playout-delay hint; 2–8 Mbit/s encoder, stepped capacity to 4 Mbit/s followed by 120 ms delay, 30 ms jitter and 2% loss. Distinct from shorter distributor qualification and the optional source-format ladder.
interpretation: Both original runs pass their existing gates. Corrected offline reanalysis also passes both, with every threshold unchanged. Original summaries and raw inputs remain intact; corrected summaries live separately and both hashes are retained.

The analyzer previously subtracted the first cumulative freeze counter in each phase, losing any increment between the preceding phase's last snapshot and the new phase's first snapshot. Two regression tests expose false acceptance when a freeze is reported only at impaired or recovery entry. The corrected report attributes each such sampling interval to its ending snapshot's phase, includes the same observation duration in the ratio denominator, and exposes the entry increment separately. This identifies reporting time, not the physical start or cause of a freeze.

Direct has 0.380 s constrained and 1.558 s impaired freezes, then no recovery freeze. TURN has 3.212 s impaired freezes (9.113%) and 0.352 s at recovery entry (0.795% of recovery observation). The TURN entry increments of 0.205 s impaired and 0.352 s recovery were absent from the original per-phase totals. No unreported improvement or freeze-free claim is inferred from a passing verdict.

Direct and TURN first reach the required recovered target after 12.124 and 13.134 s; the sustained recovery windows begin at 26.173 and 20.128 s. Both restore their encoder to the healthy range. Impaired decoding is 29.90 / 29.50 fps, with average encoder QP about 27.24.

Producer and receiver scheduling checks pass: maximum 250 ms heartbeat gaps are 259 ms direct and 261 ms TURN, with no observed steal time. Encoder maximum frame gaps across measured phases stay below 45 ms. There is no encoder-cadence failure in this pair.

These two observations do not replace the repeated release matrix or establish capture-to-display latency, recording overhead, source-format recovery or a portable CPU budget. The separate 4a0d83a MediaMTX source-capacity recovery failure remains open.
